Creative reformulation of composition as collision-aware registration problem using spatial priors from generated scenes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple baselines, quantitative metrics, and extensive qualitative results

Valuable dataset contribution of ~8,300 interactive 3D scenes to be released
Multi-part composition capability demonstrated effectively
Honest documentation of failure cases and clear identification of limitations

Heavy dependence on external proprietary models and services (Nano Banana Pro, TRELLIS2, PartField, GeoTransformer, Gemini VLM) compromises reproducibility claims
Quantitative evaluation limited to only 10 test cases; no user studies or perceptual evaluation of semantic correctness
Missing validation on actual robotic manipulation tasks despite strong robotic simulation motivation
No comparison with most related recent work (COPY-TRANSFORM-PASTE using VLM-guided composition)

Agentic refinement underspecified regarding convergence, computational cost, and success rates
Critical ablation studies missing: removing Stage 2, varying β(k) schedule, comparing registration methods

Dataset validation limited: no inter-observer metrics, composition diversity analysis, or quality assessment of physical plausibility

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap: existing 3D generation produces fused geometry lacking object-object spatial relationships, which is critical for robotic simulation
Comprehensive and thoughtful two-stage composition pipeline combining global-to-local registration with SDF-based collision-aware optimization, with principled β(k) scheduling
Creative agentic refinement strategy using VLM-based semantic-level correction to handle severe geometric mismatches from 2D occlusions that rigid transformation alone cannot fix

Extensive empirical validation: 150 test cases with quantitative metrics (CLIP, human/VLM ratings, geometric intersection), ablation study showing component contributions, and 140+ supplementary results
Significant dataset contribution: ~8,300 compositional 3D scenes across 9 categories with flexible reference meshes
Clear, well-structured presentation with effective figures demonstrating pipeline design and qualitative superiority over baselines
Training-free approach avoiding large-scale data requirements; works with both manually-modeled and generated assets
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines established techniques (OBB, GeoTransformer, scale-aware ICP, SDF optimization) without significant algorithmic innovation

Critical reproducibility issues: heavy dependence on closed-source proprietary tools (Nano Banana Pro for image generation, Gemini 3 Pro for VLM refinement, TRELLIS2 for 3D reconstruction), severely limiting reproducibility despite promised code release

Incomplete physical validity evaluation: geometric intersection metrics (Eqs. 4-5) only measure spatial overlap, not true physical plausibility; no validation in actual physics engines (PyBullet, PhysX); ignores mass, friction, center-of-mass factors critical for robotic applications

Insufficient analysis of spatial guidance quality: method relies on PartField-segmented meshes acknowledged to contain 'holes and geometric artifacts', but robustness to these artifacts lacks empirical validation; no sensitivity analysis on guidance quality impact

Dataset construction unclear: selection criterion from ~10,000 to ~8,300 candidates not specified; dataset generation process unspecified (same pipeline?); missing quality metrics, inter-annotator agreement, bias analysis

Agentic refinement under-analyzed: max 5 iterations appears arbitrary without justification; no analysis of convergence, iteration distribution, or failure modes; success entirely dependent on VLM quality

Scalability concerns with sequential composition: multi-part scenes require N-1 pipeline passes for N objects with potential error accumulation; no computational cost analysis or timing information provided

Evaluation limitations: only 150 test cases for quantitative evaluation (relatively small); ~2.3% failure rate on edge cases (Figure 7, 9) without proposed mitigation strategies; no physics simulator validation
Limited scope: declared limitation to 'daily objects'; most test cases appear relatively simple; applicability to complex robotic scenarios or fine-grained components (screws, tight joints) unclear

Hyperparameter choices lack justification: λ=0.003, kmax=100, βmax=3.0, max iterations=5 appear empirically chosen; claimed robustness 'within reasonable range' without sensitivity analysis or ablation studies
Potential biases in evaluation: VLM ratings (Qwen3) used as metric without demonstrating consistency with human ratings; missing comparisons with other optimization-based composition baselines
Methodological gap: method relies on PartField guidance containing acknowledged artifacts—mechanism for robustness unexplained; no analysis of complete PartField failures

strengths: Well-motivated problem of generating collision-aware compositional 3D scenes relevant to robotics simulation
Comprehensive pipeline design combining registration, SDF-based optimization, and VLM-driven refinement
Training-free approach enabling generalization beyond training data constraints
Extensive qualitative results with clear multi-view visualizations demonstrating diverse working examples
Ablation studies (Table 3) validating design choices including GeoTransformer, SDF term, and agentic refinement loop
Large-scale dataset contribution of 8,300 compositional scenes across 9 object categories
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: global-to-local registration combines existing techniques (OBB, GeoTransformer, ICP) without significant innovation; SDF collision optimization uses standard penalty formulation; VLM refinement is a simple wrapper around existing models

Critical gap: claims of 'physically plausible' composition are not validated with physics engine simulation (PyBullet, MuJoCo); only collision detection demonstrated—no stability analysis, gravity validation, or dynamics testing

Cascade dependencies on external proprietary models (Nano Banana Pro, TRELLIS2, Gemini 3 Pro, PartField) severely impact reproducibility and introduce error propagation; acknowledged TRELLIS2 mesh holes corrupt spatial guidance

Significant failure modes limit practical applicability: ~10% failure rate (Figure 7), poor performance on symmetric objects (11 cases), collision-divergence in complex scenes (16 cases), and acknowledged inability to handle fine-grained components (screws, tightly coupled joints)

Insufficient experimental rigor: only 150 test cases for quantitative metrics; CLIP scores are poor composition proxies; VLM-based ratings not human evaluation; no inter-rater reliability; no confidence intervals or statistical significance testing

Fundamental architectural limitation: entire approach bottlenecked by 2D image reconstruction quality; occlusions in 2D guidance cause '3D geometric ambiguities' with only heuristic VLM-based iteration as fallback—no principled occlusion handling

Dataset has unclear quality and limited scope: 17% rejection rate without specified criteria; only 9 categories; not actually released; no inter-annotator agreement metrics; limited diversity compared to existing benchmarks

Missing critical validations: no comparison with mentioned commercial tools (Hunyuan3D, Rodin); baselines designed for different tasks making comparisons somewhat unfair; PartField baseline is somewhat strawman-like
Computational cost completely unaddressed: multiple model inferences (Nano Banana Pro, TRELLIS2 twice, PartField, potentially 5 VLM iterations) but no timing information provided

Hyperparameter choices unjustified: lambda=0.003, beta_max=3.0, max 5 iterations lack principled justification or sensitivity analysis; beta schedule is simple linear increase without exploring alternatives

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical scarcity of interactive 3D compositional assets for robotic simulation
Clever technical insight leveraging spatial priors from 2D image generation to guide 3D composition via structured registration

Sound mathematical formulation with principled two-stage pipeline: global-to-local registration (Stage 1) followed by SDF-based collision-aware optimization (Stage 2) with progressive weighting schedule

Comprehensive experimental validation: 150 test cases with multiple metrics (CLIP scores, human/VLM ratings, geometric intersection rates), proper ablation study validating each component, and multi-view renderings
Quantitatively strong improvements over baselines (e.g., surface intersection rate 0.69×10⁻³ vs. 22.18×10⁻³ for PartField+RANSAC)
Valuable dataset contribution: 8,300+ compositional 3D scenes promised to be released, addressing genuine data scarcity
Clear presentation with excellent visual illustrations and comprehensive appendix including failure analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—primarily combines existing techniques (GeoTransformer, ICP, SDF optimization); core insight of spatial guidance is clever but relatively incremental
Heavy dependence on proprietary/closed-source models (Nano Banana Pro/Gemini, TRELLIS2) severely compromises reproducibility and long-term utility as underlying models evolve
Indirect spatial guidance mechanism: using PartField segmentation (which intentionally contains holes/artifacts) as supervision is problematic; limited robustness analysis for poor segmentations

Non-trivial failure rate (~21% on 140 test cases) with acknowledged limitations (geometric symmetry, severe occlusions) but insufficient quantitative failure analysis and no systematic breakdown by object category

Experimental evaluation gaps: only 150 quantitative test cases; CLIP scores measure semantic alignment rather than geometric quality; surface/volume metrics measure non-penetration but not physical plausibility (stability, balance); no physics simulation validation despite Sim2Real motivation
Pipeline brittleness: errors in TRELLIS2-generated Mscene propagate downstream with no error detection/correction mechanism; explicit supervision by potentially flawed 3D priors

Limited scope and applicability: acknowledged struggles with fine-grained components; only handles daily objects; sequential multi-part composition scalability unclear; no robot experiments despite motivation
Hyperparameter selection appears arbitrary (λ=0.003, β_max=3.0) with limited sensitivity analysis; authors claim robustness 'within reasonable range' without evidence
Computational efficiency not analyzed: single H200 GPU mentioned but no timing comparisons; agentic loop cost with 5 iterations of editing+reconstruction not quantified
Missing critical ablations: no comparison of GeoTransformer with alternative registration methods; limited analysis of when/why agentic refinement succeeds or fails beyond visual examples
